ex.en: This neighborhood is safe even at night.
Is it a safe place for kids to play?
The plane arrived safely.

note: Usually 알려 주다 (tell me) or humble 알려 드리다.

ex.en: Let me know when you arrive.
I'll let you know as soon as the results come out.
I told Mom the news first.
Check your text messages.
I double-checked the reservation time.
Could you check the bill, please?

note: 힘내세요! = Hang in there! / Cheer up!

ex.en: I'm so tired today that I have no energy.
You'll do great on the test. Hang in there!
Minho is really strong.

note: 출장 가다 = to go on a business trip.

ex.en: I'm going on a business trip to Busan next week.
My husband is on a business trip right now.
Have a good business trip!
Do you put sugar in your coffee?
Did you put an umbrella in your bag?
Please insert your card here.

note: Used to address a group; already polite, so no -님.

ex.en: Hello, everyone!
Everyone, please be quiet for a moment.

ex.s: 오늘 와 주신 여러분 모두 감사합니다.
ex.en: Thank you, everyone, for coming today.
I'm very interested in Korean culture.
Dining culture differs from country to country.
Our company doesn't have a culture of team dinners.

note: 물론이죠! = Of course!

ex.en: Of course! Let's go together.
Of course I'll help too.
Sure, it's expensive, but the taste is the best.
I want to learn cooking skills.

ex.s: 컴퓨터 기술이 있으면 일자리 찾기 쉬워요.
ex.en: With computer skills, it's easy to find a job.
Phone technology has really improved lately.

note: Not for people's height: use 키가 크다.

ex.en: That mountain is really high.
Housing prices in Seoul are too high.
My fever is a bit high today.
What time does class end?
I'll call you when the meeting is over.
Is the movie already over?
I'll definitely come again next time.
Be sure to take your medicine.
Be sure to come to the party tomorrow!
What does this word mean?
What do you mean by that?
I looked up the meaning in the dictionary.
How much are these shoes?
Prices are a bit high here.
I compared hotel prices.
It's been raining nonstop since morning.
The baby keeps crying.
I kept calling, but you didn't pick up.

ex.s: 우리 엄마 아빠는 서로 정말 사랑해요.
ex.en: My mom and dad really love each other.
Grandma, I love you! Stay healthy.
I married the person I love.

note: Casual: 아빠. Someone else's father: 아버님.

ex.en: My father works at a bank.
When is your father's birthday?
I went fishing with my father over the weekend.
Please close the door.
What time does the bank open?
Someone's knocking on the door.

note: ㄷ-irregular: 물어요, 물었어요. Often 물어보다.

ex.en: I didn't know the way, so I asked people.
Can I ask you something?
I asked the teacher about the homework.
I always drink coffee in the morning.
Ji-woo is always smiling.
Thanks for always helping me.
I don't believe that.
I can't believe it!
Don't worry. Please trust me.
The internet here is so slow.
I bought plane tickets online.
Is the internet free at the hotel?

note: For tools and objects, 쓰다 or 사용하다 is more common.

ex.en: I take the subway to work.

ex.s: 이 카드는 편의점에서도 이용할 수 있어요.
ex.en: You can use this card at convenience stores too.
The gym is open for use from 6 a.m.
How are you feeling today?
The weather is nice, so I'm in a good mood.
Hearing that upset me.

note: Intransitive (the door opens); 열다 = to open something.

ex.en: The door won't open.

ex.s: 이 병이 안 열려요. 좀 도와줄래요?
ex.en: This bottle won't open. Can you help me?
A festival is being held in the park this weekend.
Your face is red. Are you okay?
I wash my face when I get up.
It's good to see you after so long.

note: ㅅ-irregular: 지어요, 지었어요.

ex.en: What did you name your puppy?
Grandma named the baby.
They built that building last year.
We're almost there.
I'm almost done with my homework.
I hardly drink coffee these days.

note: More formal than 지금.

ex.en: I'm currently living in Seoul.
The current time is 3 p.m.
Mr. Kim is currently in a meeting.
As expected, Mom's kimchi is the best.
As expected, it's crowded because it's the weekend.
I think so too.
Wash your hands first.
I'm going to head out first.
Please go ahead and eat first.

note: -(으)ㄴ/는 편이에요 = I tend to… / it's rather…

ex.en: I tend to go to bed early.
This restaurant is on the cheap side.
I'm always on my younger sibling's side.
What book are you reading these days?
I borrowed a book from the library.
This book is really interesting.
What's that movie about?
Please email me what was covered in the meeting.
The book's content was a bit difficult.

note: Casual; say 아니요 politely. Also starts a correction or surprise.

ex.en: No, that's not what I mean.
What, it's already ten?
"Hungry?" "Nah, I'm fine."

note: Use native numbers: 한 살, 스무 살. 살이 찌다 = gain weight.

ex.en: How old are you?
Our daughter is five years old.
I've put on some weight lately.
I'll step out for a moment.
What time do you leave the house?
I'm going out to eat with friends tonight.

note: Also means 'pear' (homonym). 배고프다 = to be hungry.

ex.en: My stomach really hurts.
I ate a lot, so I'm full.
We took a boat to the island.

note: 그럼요! = Of course!

ex.en: See you tomorrow, then.
Then what should we eat?
It's raining? Then I'll take an umbrella.

note: Covers any clinic, not only large hospitals.

ex.en: I went to the doctor because of a cold.
Until what time is the clinic open?
Grandpa was admitted to the hospital.

en: to fall, drop; to run out
note: Also 시험에 떨어지다 = to fail an exam.

ex.en: My phone fell on the floor.
The temperature dropped a lot today.
We're out of milk at home.
This cake is very good.
I'm very busy today.
Minho sings very well.

note: More formal than 아주 or 정말; common in writing and announcements.

ex.en: It's going to be very cold tomorrow.
Thank you very much for your help.
This issue is very important.
Most of my friends are married.
I'm usually at home on weekends.
Most stores open at 10.

note: ㄹ drops before ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ: 여세요, 엽니다.

ex.en: Please open the window.
The store opens at 9 a.m.
Can I open the present now?

en: to raise; to put up, post

ex.en: Please put your luggage up on the shelf.
This restaurant raised its prices again.
I posted the photo I took yesterday on Instagram.
Is this seat free?
A window seat, please.
There are four of us. Do you have a table?

note: 꿈을 꾸다 = to have a dream.

ex.en: I had a strange dream last night.
My dream is to travel the world.
Sweet dreams!

note: 도움이 되다 = to be helpful.

ex.en: That was a big help. Thank you.
If you need help, tell me.

ex.s: 이 앱이 한국어 공부에 도움이 돼요.
ex.en: This app helps with studying Korean.
Who's your favorite actor?

ex.s: 이 드라마 배우들이 연기를 정말 잘해요.
ex.en: The actors in this drama are really good.
I saw a famous actor at a restaurant.

note: 사업하다 = to run a business.

ex.en: My father runs a small business.
How's business going?
I started a business with a friend.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 쉬워요, 쉬운.

ex.en: This problem is easier than I thought.
Hangul is easy to learn.
It's easy to get from the station to the hotel.

note: Someone else's son: 아드님 (honorific).

ex.en: My son just started college.
I have two sons.
I play soccer with my son on weekends.
What sports do you like?
When it comes to sports, I only like watching.
I watched the game at a sports bar with friends.

note: Common: 서비스센터 (repair center), 고객센터 (customer service).

ex.en: My phone broke, so I went to the service center.
Try calling customer service.
I'm learning to swim at the local sports center.

en: to do so; to say so
note: Common forms: 그래요? (Really?), 왜 그래요? (What's wrong?)

ex.en: What's wrong? Did something happen?
Please don't do that.
Mom said it's going to rain tomorrow.
I'm really happy these days.
I'm happiest when I'm with my family.
Happy birthday! Have a happy day.

note: Casual 인생 + noun = the best ever (인생 영화).

ex.en: Life is short.
This was the best trip of my life.

ex.s: 이 집 떡볶이는 제 인생 떡볶이예요.
ex.en: This place's tteokbokki is the best I've ever had.

ex.s: 이 셔츠 다른 사이즈로 바꿀 수 있어요?
ex.en: Can I exchange this shirt for a different size?
I changed my phone password.

ex.s: 자리 좀 바꿔 주실 수 있어요?
ex.en: Could you switch seats with me?
I like fruit, especially strawberries.
I'm especially tired today.
This restaurant's kimchi stew is especially good.

note: 해외여행 = a trip abroad.

ex.en: Have you ever traveled abroad?
My younger sibling works abroad.

ex.s: 이 카드는 해외에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
ex.en: You can use this card abroad too.

note: Opposite: 유료 (paid). Never 'free' as in free time.

ex.en: Parking is free.
Water is free of charge.

ex.s: 이 앱은 한 달 동안 무료예요.
ex.en: This app is free for a month.

note: Used for struck instruments and racket sports: 피아노를 치다, 테니스를 치다.

ex.en: I play tennis every weekend.
My daughter plays the piano well.
My friend playfully hit my shoulder.

note: 아래층 = downstairs.

ex.en: The cat hid under the bed.
The restroom is one floor down.
The key is under the flower pot.

en: to be better; to get well
note: ㅅ-irregular: 나아요, 나았어요, 나으세요.

ex.en: This one is better than that one.
The subway is better than a taxi.
I hope your cold gets better soon.

note: Your own feelings; for others use 싫어하다.

ex.en: I hate rainy days.
I don't feel like going out today.
I don't like cucumber. Please leave it out.
I have a terrible headache.
Where does it hurt?

ex.s: 아이가 아파서 오늘 회사에 못 가요.
ex.en: My kid is sick, so I can't go to work today.

en: to take charge of; to keep (for someone)
note: Also 냄새를 맡다 = to smell something.

ex.en: I'll take care of this task.
Ji-woo is in charge of this project.

ex.s: 짐 좀 맡아 주실 수 있어요?
ex.en: Could you keep my bags for me?
Wow, that outfit looks great!
The view here is really amazing.
Thanks for the wonderful gift.
Come quick! The movie's starting.
We're late. Shall we walk a bit faster?
Time goes by really fast.

note: Counter with native numbers: 한 가지, 두 가지. 여러 가지 = various.

ex.en: Could I ask you one favor?

ex.s: 이 셔츠는 세 가지 색이 있어요.
ex.en: This shirt comes in three colors.

ex.s: 여행 가서 여러 가지 음식을 먹어 봤어요.
ex.en: I tried all kinds of food on the trip.

note: Spelled 바라요, not the common misspelling 바래요.

ex.en: I hope you get better soon.
I hope you get a good result.
I wish you both happiness.

note: Konglish: 서비스 also means a free extra from a shop.

ex.en: The service at this hotel is really good.
The internet service is down again.
The owner gave us dumplings on the house.
My grandmother lives in a small village.
This village is quiet and pretty.
We stayed two nights in a seaside village.
Who's your favorite soccer player?
Our son plays basketball for his school.
The players are coming onto the field.

note: 준비하다 = to prepare. 준비됐어요? = Are you ready?

ex.en: Are you all ready?
I'll take care of making dinner.
Are your trip preparations going well?

note: In speech usually 뭐; 무엇 sounds formal.

ex.en: How can I help you?
If you're curious about anything, just ask.
Above all, health is the most important thing.
I have a question!
If you have questions, ask anytime.
I got a lot of tough questions in the interview.

note: 화가 나다 = to get angry; 화내다 = to get mad at someone.

ex.en: Why are you so angry?
Please don't be mad. I made a mistake.
The traffic is so bad it's making me mad.

note: Humble form of 우리; not for Korea itself (say 우리나라).

ex.en: Come over to our place.
Our company starts at 9.
Our child is seven years old.
Until when is the sale?
It's exam period, so I'm really busy.
The weather was nice during the trip.

note: 감사합니다 is more formal than 고마워요.

ex.en: Thank you so much for your help.
Thank you for inviting me.
I sent my teacher a thank-you text.
I work out three times a week.
I was on Jeju Island for a week.
The package took a week to arrive.
How's life in Korea?
College life is really fun.
Work life is a bit hard.

note: Males say 형, females say 오빠. Also for close older male friends.

ex.en: I have one older brother.
Bro, want to grab something to eat?
My older brother works in the U.S.

note: Also 시계를 차다 = to wear a watch.

ex.en: The parking lot is already full.

ex.s: 이 식당은 항상 손님으로 가득 차 있어요.
ex.en: This restaurant is always packed with customers.
The child kicked the ball hard.

note: 시작하다 = to start something.

ex.en: The movie is starting soon.
They say the rainy season starts next week.
Class starts at nine.

note: 사고가 나다 = an accident happens.

ex.en: There was a car accident on the street.
Traffic is really bad because of an accident.

ex.s: 다친 데 없어요? 큰 사고 날 뻔했어요.
ex.en: Are you hurt? That was almost a serious accident.

note: Address and refer to them as 교수님.

ex.en: Professor, I have a question.
My older brother is a university professor.
The professor gave us a lot of homework.
I was so surprised at that moment.
Our wedding day was the happiest moment.
The moment I opened the door, the cat ran out.

note: -에 관심이 있다 = to be interested in.

ex.en: I'm very interested in cooking.
What are you into these days?
Thank you for your interest.
The train already left.
We're leaving on a trip early tomorrow morning.
It's been ten years since I left my hometown.

note: Someone else's daughter: 따님 (honorific).

ex.en: My daughter is learning to swim these days.
I have two daughters.
I went shopping with my daughter.

note: Konglish: means any website, not just its main page.

ex.en: Check the website for details.
I made a reservation on the restaurant's website.
What's the company's website address?
I couldn't sleep properly last night.
Did you really understand this explanation?
Please eat proper meals.
This café has a nice vibe.

ex.s: 오늘 좋은 일이 있을 것 같은 느낌이에요.
ex.en: I have a feeling something good will happen today.
What was your first impression of him?
How many dollars is this?
I exchanged dollars for won at the airport.
It's five dollars for a cup of coffee.

note: For children or someone younger; 젊다 = young (adult).

ex.en: My younger sibling is three years younger than me.
I lived in Busan when I was little.

ex.s: 아이가 아직 어려서 혼자 못 가요.
ex.en: The kid is still young, so they can't go alone.

note: 이쪽 = this way, 저쪽 = over there.

ex.en: Come this way, please.
The restroom is over there.
Open your book to page 50.
